discoveries: (1) `command.py:233-234` decides whether to hand the pytest plugin to the runs by checking `settings.get(accepted_reds|load_sensitive)`, which reads the **path map's** keys. While the keys stay as exact copies this changes nothing. Once the owner removes them, the close would stop collecting per-test results, so reds would no longer be judged by the record files' lists: accepted reds would stop being covered and load-sensitive re-runs would stop. That fails closed (reds refuse) but loses the quarantine. (2) W1-01's support (`w1_01_support.acceptance_exemptions`) reads the exemptions from the path map itself, so it stops seeing the exemptions once the key is dropped. (3) Exemption-file findings travel in `judged_history`'s `refused`, because that is the only channel `command.py` refuses on. As a side effect a broken exemptions file also turns the product-traceability check red. (4) `gates.RECORD_PREFIXES`, the paths a decision-record commit may change, does not include `governance/project/records/`. I left it, as policy I was not asked to change. (5) The schemas require each list's fields, so an entry missing one invalidates the whole file. That is stricter than the old per-entry finding, and it fails closed.
